about: Hand-written rotation guides for the paladin's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: Retribution in a raid twists seals: you swap between **Seal of Righteousness** and **Seal of Command** around every swing so each hit carries both, judge **Seal of Righteousness** on cooldown, and give the remaining global cooldowns to **Consecration**, **Holy Strike** and, under 20% health, **Hammer of Wrath**.
why: Only one seal can be active, so keeping up two seals means a twist: with **Twist of Light**, replacing a seal leaves an Echo of it that your next melee swing applies. The full rotation casts **Seal of Righteousness** in the last 0.4 seconds before each swing and **Seal of Command** after the swing, in any global cooldown that **Hammer of Wrath**, **Consecration** and **Holy Strike** do not need: about 14 and 12 times a minute. Opening with **Seal of Command** means your very first swing already carries both.

Press **Judgement** every time it is ready while **Seal of Righteousness** is up, whether or not the short list shows it. It is off the global cooldown, comes back every 8 seconds with **Improved Judgement**, no longer uses up your seal in Forever, and **Sanctified Judgement** returns 60% of the seal's mana cost; in the simulator the judgement of **Seal of Righteousness** is about an eighth of your damage. If it comes off cooldown while **Seal of Command** is up, judge anyway.

**Hammer of Wrath** goes first once the boss is below 20% health: with 2 points in **Instrument of Law** it is instant, it comes back every 6 seconds, and at about 500 Holy damage plus a share of your spell damage it is your biggest single hit.

**Consecration** comes before **Holy Strike** while you have at least a quarter of your mana: on a single boss it deals 312 Holy damage over 8 seconds plus a share of your spell damage, about a sixth of your damage in the simulator, and **Holy Conduit** makes it 40% cheaper.

**Holy Strike** sits last but is not a real filler: it has a 10-second cooldown, so press it whenever it is ready (20 mana, and **Sacred Arbiter** adds 20% to it). The global cooldowns between your other buttons go to the seal swaps.

**Seal of Command** is always rank 4: every rank adds the same 70% of weapon damage, rank 4 costs 30 mana less, and the simulator measured it 0.3% better than rank 5. When mana runs low the full rotation steps down: **Seal of Righteousness** rank 7 below half mana, **Seal of Command** rank 2 below 30%, a rank 1 **Consecration** below a quarter, and no seal swaps at all below 15%.
caveats: The twist rests on the simulator's reading of **Twist of Light**: every Echo you have up fires on the next swing, so a swing after both swaps applies **Seal of Righteousness** twice (the seal and its Echo) and **Seal of Command**'s chance once. If the game allows only one Echo per swing, one swap per swing, alternating the two seals, does the same work with half the global cooldowns: check it at launch.

All those swaps cost mana, even 20% cheaper with **Twist of Light**. The full-raid numbers assume the raid's **Blessing of Wisdom**, Mana Spring and other paladins' judgements of **Seal of Wisdom** and **Seal of the Crusader** on the boss; with only your own buffs the simulator keeps **Seal of Righteousness** up and twists on every swing only while your mana is above about two thirds.

Forever weakens ranks far below your level, and the simulator applies an assumed formula (TBC's) since 2026-10-09. **Seal of Command** rank 4 and **Seal of Righteousness** rank 7 are close enough to 60 to lose nothing, but rank 1 **Consecration** keeps only a bit over half of its spell damage bonus, so it is a low-mana stopgap only; the game may also lower a low rank's chance to trigger effects, which no simulator models.
Several targets: only **Consecration** spreads (its bonus damage hits the first four enemies in it); your seals, judgements and **Holy Strike** stay on one target.
The full rotation also has a **Holy Shock** line (after **Holy Strike**) for builds that take it, worth several percent there in the simulator; this build has no **Holy Shock**, so skip it.
diverge: If you cannot time your swings (no swing timer, high latency), skip the swaps: keep **Seal of Righteousness** up, judge it on cooldown and press **Consecration** and **Holy Strike**. How much that costs on the current beta build was not measured.

Against an Undead or Demon boss, add **Exorcism** on cooldown (15 seconds, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**): it hits harder than **Holy Strike**. The simulator's target is an Elemental, so where it fits best was not measured.
When you have to leave melee range, keep pressing **Judgement** (10 yards) and, under 20%, **Hammer of Wrath** (30 yards); your seals only work on swings.

leveling.plan: Retribution levels with one seal: **Seal of Command** before each pull, **Judgement** and **Holy Strike** on cooldown, **Hammer of Wrath** to finish, and your mana kept for judgements, the hammer and heals instead of **Consecration**.
why: **Seal of Command** goes up before each pull (from level 20; **Seal of Righteousness** before that) and lasts 30 seconds, longer than most fights. It adds a Holy hit of 70% of your weapon damage about 7 times a minute, so a slow two-hander suits it; this build has no **Twist of Light**, so there is no seal swapping while leveling.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready: **Judgement** is off the global cooldown and comes back every 8 seconds with both points of **Improved Judgement** (levels 24 and 26), **Sanctified Judgement** (21-23) returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time, and **Sacred Arbiter** (25) adds 20% to **Holy Strike**. The open search found **Sanctified Judgement** the build's most valuable talent at 60 (about 3.3 seconds per kill without it), for the drinking it saves; then **Conviction** (15-19, about 1.7 s), **Holy Conduit** (27-28) and **Improved Seals** (40-42, about 1.4 s each).

**Consecration** is for two or more mobs. Against a single mob the fight lab's tuned rules (re-tuned from scratch on 2026-10-23) never cast it and kill about 5% faster that way: its mana costs more drinking than its damage saves.

**Hammer of Justice** doubles **Seal of Command**'s judgement: against a stunned mob it hits for 339 to 373 instead of 169 to 187 at rank 5. When both are ready and the mob has more than 30% health left, stun first, then judge; otherwise keep the stun for a caster or for when you are hurt.

**Hammer of Wrath** finishes mobs below 20% health from level 44; its 1-second cast goes away with the 2 points of **Instrument of Law** (levels 44 and 45), and **Holy Conduit** takes 40% off its mana. In the fight lab it is about 13% of the damage at 60 (measured on the hand-made 15/0/36 build, which plays the same list).

The last points (levels 48-60: **Toughness**, **Precision**, **Champion of the Light**, **Anticipation**, **Guardian's Favor**) are small: **Precision** is worth about 1.1 seconds per kill at 60, and **Guardian's Favor** does nothing in the fight lab (a spare point).

Below about a third of your health, while the mob still has a quarter of its own: **Divine Protection** (8 seconds immune, but you cannot attack) with **Holy Light** inside it, or **Hammer of Justice** and heal during the stun; **Flash of Light** below a quarter, **Lay on Hands** below 15%. Against same-level mobs the fight lab almost never needed these. Between fights heal back to 80%; the tuned rules drink only below 15% of your mana.
caveats: Several mobs: **Consecration** hits all of them and its bonus damage goes to the first four in it, so it earns its mana there. The fight lab's three-mob runs still played without it, so the gain is unmeasured.

Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** (instant, 30 yards, 15-second cooldown, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**) hits them hard, and **Holy Wrath** handles packs. The fight lab has no Undead or Demon mobs, so neither was measured.
diverge: A mob that stands back and casts: **Hammer of Justice** (10 yards) stops the cast; the fight lab uses it that way.
A mob that runs at low health: **Hammer of Wrath** (30 yards) finishes it, or **Hammer of Justice** holds it.

raid.plan: Most of your threat is Holy damage, and **Righteous Fury** makes it 90% more threat. Keep **Holy Shield** up, judge **Seal of Righteousness** on cooldown and press **Consecration** and **Holy Strike** whenever they are ready; **Templar's Bulwark** and **Lay on Hands** are your big defensive buttons.
why: Before the pull: **Righteous Fury** (it lasts 30 minutes, and **Improved Righteous Fury** and **Iron Creed** only work while it is up), then **Seal of Righteousness** and **Holy Shield** in the last seconds, so the first hits already meet both.

**Holy Shield** lasts 10 seconds and comes back every 10, so keep it up all fight: 30% more block for 4 blocks, and every block deals Holy damage with 20% extra threat and can trigger **Redoubt** and **Shield Specialization**'s mana. The simulator measured 1.3% more tank value with it at the top of the list.

Press **Judgement** on cooldown, whether or not the short list shows it: it is off the global cooldown, judges **Seal of Righteousness** for about a tenth of your threat, and no longer uses up the seal in Forever. Judging every time it is ready, instead of only before the seal runs out, measured 4.3% more tank value; **Swift Judgement** goes right after a **Judgement**, because it finishes the cooldown and makes the next one free.

**Consecration** and **Holy Strike** fill the rest: **Consecration** threatens everything standing in it, and **Holy Strike** with **Iron Creed** makes 25% more threat and cuts your damage taken by 10% for 6 seconds. Refresh **Seal of Righteousness** when it has about a second left.

**Templar's Bulwark** sits at the top because the simulator's 3-minute fight fits one use: it absorbs damage equal to your maximum health for 8 seconds, off the global cooldown, and using it at the pull measured 1.4% more tank value. It applies Forbearance for a minute, which locks you out of **Divine Protection**, **Divine Shield** and **Blessing of Protection**.

**Lay on Hands** is last in the list with no health condition: in the simulator's fights nobody heals you, and casting it whenever nothing else is ready measured 0.4% more tank value than keeping it for 10% health (8% more than not using it). It heals you for your maximum health but drains all your mana, and its cooldown is 20 minutes: in a raid with healers, keep it for when you are about to die.
caveats: The simulator tanks with **Seal of Righteousness**. **Seal of Fury** (35 Holy damage a swing, plus an absorb of half of it while you hold a shield) is not part of its tuned rotation, so whether it is better for you was not measured.

Mana: you run dry for a few seconds of each 3-minute fight in the simulator. **Consecration** is the expensive button (565 mana before **Holy Conduit**); blocks give mana back through **Shield Specialization** and judgements through **Sanctified Judgement**.
The simulator measures one boss. **Consecration** and **Holy Shield** work on everything that hits you; **Holy Strike** and **Judgement** only on your target.
diverge: To taunt (a tank swap, a loose add), put up **Seal of Fury** and judge: its judgement taunts for 4 seconds. Use **Swift Judgement** if **Judgement** is on cooldown, then go back to **Seal of Righteousness**.
Hold **Templar's Bulwark** for a known damage spike or a healer death when the fight has one: the simulator spends it at the pull only because its fight fits a single use.

Undead or Demon packs: **Holy Wrath** (a 2-second cast) hits and stuns every Undead and Demon within 20 yards, and **Exorcism** hits one hard. Neither was measured: the simulator's boss is an Elemental.

leveling.plan: Protection levels behind a shield: **Seal of Fury** turns half of its Holy damage into an absorb, blocks and judgements pay your mana back, and **Judgement**, **Holy Strike**, **Consecration** and, at 60, **Holy Shield** do the damage. The order takes Retribution's mana talents first (levels 10-25) and Protection from 26, with **Holy Shield** last at 60. Over levels 20-60 it is about 9% slower per kill than the Retribution page in the fight lab (30.8 against 28.2 seconds).
why: **Seal of Fury** before each pull: at rank 7 (level 58) it adds 35 Holy damage to every swing, and with a shield each swing also gives you an absorb of half that damage. **Shield Specialization** (levels 36-38) adds block value and returns 4% of your mana on a block, at most once every 3 seconds, and **Improved Seal of Fury** (40) 60 mana each time such an absorb is used up; the open search values them at about 2.2 and 1.8 seconds per kill at 60.

**Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready, with **Swift Judgement** (level 41) right after a **Judgement**: it finishes the cooldown and makes the next one free. **Sanctified Judgement** (20-22) returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time you judge: the open search found it the build's most valuable talent at 60 (about 2.7 seconds per kill without it).

**Holy Shield** (level 60) whenever it is down: 30% more block for 10 seconds or 4 blocks, and 221 Holy damage for each block at rank 3. The fight lab casts it about twice a kill at 60 and values it at about 2.4 seconds per kill.

**Consecration** only while your mana is above 60% and the mob has more than 30% health, a hand-set rule the fight lab plays (no search has tuned the Protection list). **Holy Conduit** (levels 24 and 45) makes it and **Hammer of Wrath** 40% cheaper (about 2.3 seconds per kill at 60). **Hammer of Wrath** finishes mobs below 20% health from level 44; this build has no **Instrument of Law**, so it keeps its 1-second cast.

**Reckoning** (53-57): a block or a critical hit taken can store an extra attack (up to 4), all released with your next swing; about 1.4 seconds per kill at 60. **Redoubt** (27-30 and 33) and **One-Handed Weapon Specialization** (46-47 and 50) are worth about 0.9 seconds each.

Keep **Righteous Fury** up even alone: **Iron Creed** (58-59: **Holy Strike** cuts your damage taken for 6 seconds) only works while it is on, and the fight lab keeps it up all the time. This build takes no **Improved Righteous Fury**.

Below about a third of your health (the mob above a fifth): **Templar's Bulwark** first (level 49; an absorb as large as your health for 8 seconds), then **Holy Light** behind it. Otherwise the fight lab casts **Holy Light** only while the mob cannot hurt you: during **Divine Protection** (below 30%) or while **Hammer of Justice** holds it; **Flash of Light** below a quarter, **Lay on Hands** below 15%. Drink below 15% of your mana; you rarely need to eat.
caveats: Before level 60 skip the **Holy Shield** line, before 49 the **Templar's Bulwark** one and before 41 **Swift Judgement**: the order takes them there.
The gap to Retribution is mostly at levels 20-40 (22.9, 28.8 and 32.9 seconds per kill against 19.7, 23.3 and 28.6); at 50 and 60 Protection is within about 4% (30.8 and 33.1 against 29.5 and 32.1).
**Templar's Bulwark** applies Forbearance for a minute, so **Divine Protection** is not available right after it.
Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** (instant, 15-second cooldown, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**) hits them hard. The fight lab has no such mobs, so it was not measured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.
Two or more mobs: **Consecration** hits them all; the 60% mana rule was set for single mobs, and this list was not measured on several.
Tanking a dungeon on the way: **Seal of Fury**'s judgement taunts for 4 seconds, and **Righteous Fury** makes your Holy attacks cause 90% more threat.

raid.plan: You heal with two spells: **Holy Light** on the tank, in the rank that covers what he is missing, and **Flash of Light** on everyone else. This build takes no **Holy Shock**: **Divine Favor** and **Lay on Hands** are your emergency buttons, and your critical heals pay part of their mana back.
why: Keep **Blessing of Light** on the tank: it adds up to 400 to each **Holy Light** and 115 to each **Flash of Light** he receives. Start a **Holy Light** when he is missing at least half of one and more hits are coming; in the healer lab the two spells do almost all your healing.

Downrank: cast the smallest rank that heals about what the target is missing. Forever gives ranks far below your level less of your +healing (TBC's rule, our assumption): **Holy Light** ranks 7 to 9 and **Flash of Light** ranks 5 and 6 lose nothing or almost nothing, while rank 6 **Holy Light** keeps 85% of the bonus and lower ranks less, so stay near the top.

**Flash of Light** is your raid heal and your emergency heal: the lab heals other raid members once they fall below half health, and anyone under a quarter of their health gets a **Flash of Light** first.

**Divine Favor** (2-minute cooldown) goes before a top-rank **Holy Light** on a tank who is missing most of one: a sure critical heal, which **Illumination** then refunds. **Infusion of Light** (one point) makes your next **Holy Light** within 15 seconds half a second faster after a critical **Flash of Light**.

Mana: **Illumination** returns half the base cost of each critical **Holy Light** or **Flash of Light**, **Holy Power** adds 5% crit to your heals, **Healing Light** 12% healing, and **Reverence** keeps 30% of your mana regeneration going while you cast. Drink a mana potion as soon as you are below 80% mana (after the first 45 seconds).
**Lay on Hands** is for a tank about to die (the lab uses it under 20% health): it heals him for your maximum health but drains all your mana, and its 20-minute cooldown makes it once a fight.
caveats: The healer lab is this project's model of stated assumptions: one tank under boss melee and four raid members under raid damage for five minutes, with no dispels and no spell pushback. Check its numbers at launch.

The deep search's winner (re-run 2026-10-21, about 2% more capacity than the hand draft) takes neither **Holy Shock** nor **Light's Vigil**: the healer lab measured more capacity without them. The build therefore has no group heal; **Flash of Light** on the lowest member is your answer to raid damage.
**Spiritual Focus** (one point) keeps 35% of your **Holy Light** and **Flash of Light** casts from being pushed back; the lab has no pushback, so its value there is unmeasured.
diverge: When a whole party is taking damage, heal the lowest member with **Flash of Light**; you have no group heal in this build.
**Cleanse** a harmful magic, poison or disease effect when it would cost more healing than the cast; the lab has no debuffs, so when is your call.

leveling.plan: Holy levels as a Retribution paladin first: the first 21 points (levels 10-30) go into Retribution (**Seal of Command**, **Sanctified Judgement**, **Improved Judgement**), Holy starts at 31 and **Holy Shock** comes at 51. You play the Holy list with a two-hander: **Seal of Command**, **Judgement** and **Holy Strike** on cooldown, **Hammer of Wrath** to finish, **Holy Shock** from 51. Over levels 20-60 it is about 7% slower per kill than the Retribution page in the fight lab (30.2 against 28.2 seconds).
why: Up to level 50 it plays like Retribution with **Blessing of Wisdom** instead of **Blessing of Might**: **Seal of Command** from level 20 (**Seal of Righteousness** before), **Hammer of Justice** before a **Judgement** on a mob above 30% health (the judgement hits a stunned mob twice as hard), then **Judgement** and **Holy Strike** whenever ready. The fight lab times it within about 2% of the Retribution page there (19.8, 23.6, 28.0 and 30.1 seconds per kill at 20, 30, 40 and 50, against 19.7, 23.3, 28.6 and 29.5).

**Sanctified Judgement** (levels 21-23) returns 60% of your seal's mana cost each time you judge: the open search found it the build's most valuable talent at 60 (about 2.6 seconds per kill without it), ahead of **Improved Seals** (36-38, about 1.7 s), **Holy Power** (56-60, about 1.6 s), **Conviction** (15-19) and **Improved Judgement** (24 and 26).

**Holy Shock** (level 51) at the mob as it walks in, only while your mana is above 70% and the mob has more than 10% health left (the list's hand-set rule); at rank 4 (level 56) it hits for 334 to 362 on a 10-second cooldown. With **Divine Favor** (54) ready and your health above 70%, press it first for a sure critical hit. The mana rule keeps it to about 0.6 casts per kill at 60; **Holy Power** adds 15% crit to it and to **Holy Strike**, and **Divine Precision** (52-53) 12% hit to both.

**Hammer of Wrath** below 20% health from level 44 (the tuned rules no longer skip it): this build has no **Instrument of Law**, so it keeps its 1-second cast, and **Holy Conduit** (28-29) takes 40% off its mana (about 1.2 seconds per kill at 60). No **Consecration** against a single mob: the Holy list never casts it (its mana buys more as **Holy Shock** and less drinking), so **Consecrated Ground** (55) does nothing there.

Heal in the fight once you drop below 40% health and the mob has more than a fifth left: **Holy Shock** on yourself (after **Divine Favor** if it is ready), **Divine Protection** below 30%, **Hammer of Justice**, then **Holy Light**; **Flash of Light** below a quarter, **Lay on Hands** below 15%. **Illumination** (46-50) returns half the base cost of a critical heal, **Spiritual Focus** (40 and 45) keeps 70% of your heals from being pushed back, and **Reverence** (41-43) keeps 30% of your mana regeneration going while you cast. Against same-level mobs the fight lab rarely needed these heals.
Drink below 15% of your mana (the tuned rule of 2026-10-23; the list's own default was a quarter); between fights heal back to 80% with **Holy Light** or **Flash of Light**.
caveats: From level 51, once the build has **Holy Shock**, the fight lab dresses it in caster gear (spell power and Intellect) instead of melee gear, and its time per kill jumps from 30.1 seconds at 50 to 38.5 at 60 (Retribution: 32.1). Whether melee gear would be faster at 60 for this build was not measured.

**Purifying Power** (44) does nothing in the fight lab: **Exorcism** and **Holy Wrath** are for Undead and Demons, which the lab has none of. Against them use **Exorcism** on cooldown (instant, 40% cheaper with **Holy Conduit**, a 17% shorter cooldown with **Purifying Power**); unmeasured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.
Two or more mobs: **Consecration** hits them all and **Consecrated Ground** then adds 5% to your Holy damage on them; the Holy list was not measured on several mobs with this build.
If you only want to reach 60, level as Retribution and respec at 60: its page is about 7% faster per kill over 20-60.

leveling.plan: The Prot-Ret leveling page is the stats model's pick for solo play at 60: a two-handed Retribution paladin (**Seal of Command**, **Judgement**, **Holy Strike**) whose last 16 points (levels 45-60) go into Protection. It plays the Retribution list; the fight lab's signature check times it at about 29.6 seconds per kill over levels 20-60, about 3% slower than the Retribution page in the same check (28.6).
why: Levels 10-44 are a Retribution leveling build: **Benediction** (10-14), **Conviction** (15-19), **Seal of Command** (20), **Sanctified Judgement** (21-22 and 26), **Sacred Arbiter** (25), **Improved Judgement** (27-28), **Vengeance** (30-32), **Two-Handed Weapon Specialization** (33-34), **Instrument of Law** (35-36), then **Divine Strength** and **Improved Seals** from Holy (37-44). Play it like the Retribution page: **Seal of Command** before each pull, **Judgement** and **Holy Strike** on cooldown, **Hammer of Justice** before a **Judgement** on a mob above 30% health.

No **Consecration** against a single mob: the Retribution list's tuned rules never cast it (about 5% faster kills). **Hammer of Wrath** below 20% health from level 44, instant with **Instrument of Law**. Drink below 15% of your mana.

Of the Protection points, **Precision** (50-52, 3% hit), **Anticipation** (53-54, Defense) and **Sacred Duty** (55-56, more Stamina and a shorter **Divine Protection** cooldown) work with a two-hander in the fight lab. **Pursuit of Justice** (23-24) is travel speed, which the fight lab does not model.
caveats: **Redoubt**, **Shield Specialization** and **Improved Seal of Fury** need a shield and **Seal of Fury**, and the Retribution list never presses **Swift Judgement**: with a two-hander in the Retribution list these 9 points do nothing in the fight lab. The Retribution page's build is the faster measured one.
Undead and Demons: **Exorcism** hits them hard; the fight lab has no such mobs, so it was not measured.
diverge: A mob that casts spells: **Hammer of Justice** stops the cast.
Two or more mobs: **Consecration** hits them all; the single-target rule does not apply there.
**Swift Judgement** (60) right after a **Judgement** gives you a free second one; the Retribution list does not press it, so its worth for this build is unmeasured.
If you carry a shield and **Seal of Fury** instead, play the Protection page's list: that is what these points are for (not measured for this build).
